claims.text: The Sindarin name Othrondir means "man of an underground stronghold" (othrond 'underground stronghold' + dîr 'man').
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, Christopher Tolkien (ed.), The War of the Jewels, "Part Four. Quendi and Eldar: Author's Notes to Quendi and Eldar", p. 414 (Ńote 26), from ost + rond.; J.R.R. Tolkien, Christopher Tolkien (ed.), The Lost Road and Other Writings, Part Three: "The Etymologies", p 354 (entry DER).

claims.text: Othrondir was an acquaintace of Borlas of Pen-arduin, to whom he had told about some rumors concerning a certain restlessness in Gondor. He was also the one who first used the word "canker", evidently referring to secret followers of the "Dark Tree" that was rising during the year . under the leadership of someone by the name of Herumor.
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, Christopher Tolkien (ed.), The Peoples of Middle-earth, "XVI. The New Shadow", pp. 414, 417.

claims.text:
The name was Othrondor in the first manuscript (ms. A) of the story, which was then changed to Othrondir in the following manuscripts (mss. B and C).
